sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI understands just how important a smartphone is
sources.text: Text messages, social networking, selfies — the device is integrated into every aspect of your virtual life. Text messages, social networking, selfies — the device is integrated into every aspect of your virtual life. Grand Theft Auto VI , in many ways, tries to simulate real life. And life in 2026 would not be complete without a smartphone. GTA VI understands this and makes the phone not just a central part of the experience, but an object that exists within the world. You may try to escape into a fantasy of robbing banks and fighting drug lords, but you can’t get away from texts from your mom or nagging fitness app notifications. Seeing a smartphone in a game isn’t a new phenomenon. The device has become a natural stand-in for the main menu in many games, giving players an interface that feels intuitive, because a phone is something they use every day. But the phone in GTA VI is different for a few reasons. One is that it behaves much like any other object in the game, whether it’s a gun or a bottle of beer. The action doesn’t pause when you use your phone. Instead, the game switches to a first-person viewpoint, where you can still walk around — or drive, if you’re feeling ambitious — while reading texts or flipping through a fictional version of Instagram. Rob Nelson, the co-studio head at developer Rockstar North and producer on GTA VI , says that it would’ve felt “archaic” to have a static phone that worked like those in other games, or the one in GTA V , which appeared as a pop-up at the bottom of the screen across from the minimap. “We felt that it was important to make it physical so you have to look at it and put your attention on it, including while driving,” he explains. “It’s about finding the line between realism and player convenience. But the act of being lost in your phone felt like something worth doing, even though it could mean slightly more inconvenience. In this game you are committing to using it.” (Of course, texting and driving, like much of what you do in GTA VI , is both very dangerous and very illegal.) You have to interact with the phone in the game constantly. Often the story plays out through phone calls and text messages, and you have a surprisingly large array of apps to use that serve a real purpose in the game. You manage your money in a banking app, use a rideshare app when you need a lift, track your workouts in a fitness app, scroll through a social network complete with comments and the ability to like posts, and sideload an AI tool that scans nearby cars so you can see how easy they’ll be to steal. You can even change the wallpaper and ringtone. ( GTA VI has two main characters that you swap between, and each has their own phone, though they’re functionally identical.) What’s most impressive is how all of these apps interact with each other. For instance, after pulling off a major heist, a friend might text you a news story about it, asking “was this you!?” You can then click the link, open up the news app, and read an actual article about what went down. These kinds of interactions can be functional, like when another character texts you a location, which you can then add to your map so the GPS can guide you there. Other times, they add texture to the world or depth to the characters. GTA VI is a love story about two criminals named Jason and Lucia, and you play as both. At one point, while controlling Lucia, I got a text asking for a selfie. I opened up the camera, shot a pic of Lucia drinking a latte, and sent it over. Jason replied immediately — and their relationship got a boost. Phones are so fully integrated into the game that they can even interrupt the characters’ sleep. At the end of each day, you can click on a bed to rest for the night. But neither Jason nor Lucia will instantly fall asleep when you do — instead, they’ll sit down and pull out their phone, and you have the option to doomscroll or catch up on texts instead of going to sleep right away. Nelson says that this was implemented because the developers wanted to include the ability for the characters to sit on the bed at night, much like a real couple in a shared living space might do. “We needed something to do aside from just sitting there staring at nothing,” he says. If nothing else, GTA VI ’s phone shows how alike we all are: Even bank robbers being hunted by the police can’t seem to stop scrolling. “Phones are a constant part of our lives,” Nelson says of the evolution, “even more than they were in 2013.”

sources.text: The Grand Theft Auto series has a propensity for memorable protagonists. Tommy Vercetti in Vice City, CJ in San Andreas, and Niko Bellic in 4 are key to what makes their respective entries so beloved. The same is true for Michael, Franklin, and Trevor regarding 5, and it should come as no surprise that GTA 6 pays an all-too-appropriate nod to the trio who led the previous entry in the series. While driving around Leonida and enjoying the podcast Vice City True Stories, you'll eventually start hearing about a few familiar names. It's a true crime podcast, because of course it is, and one of the subjects is a certain bank heist you'll know plenty about if you've completed the main story of Grand Theft Auto 5. Specifically, Trevor's pal Wade Hebert, and the suspicious deaths of Floyd and Deborah. The hosts are skeptical of his connection to Trevor, and how protective he was of Trevor's two partners in crime. A whole segment's been clipped on Twitter by DiscussingFilm if you can't play just now. "Could it be that the photograph was actually of three dangerous criminals? Criminals who knew how to handle a knife or a gun?" the host ponders. "Taking out Floyd and Deborah might have been as easy for them as it is for me to take no notice of failed auditions or final demands for payment." Oh, you don't know the half of it. These three men made Los Santos their playground, and they did it over and over again for years - though for you it would've been a much shorter period of time. "There were so many more questions about Michael, Franklin, and Wade's BFF," she continues. "What did Wade mean about robbing all them banks?" What did he mean, indeed. It's a delightfully meta way to tie the two games together, setting things up for further elaboration whenever Rockstar wants to go deeper. Since the game has podcasts, I hope the intention is to continue recording episodes and keep the radio selection updated. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more When you have over two billion US dollars in revenue right at launch, that kind of investment seems easy. Even if that's not what happens, it's good someone's scoping out the activities of those three. They aren't to be trusted, no matter how friendly they can come across. sources.text: Looks like Lawrence Sullivan settled his differences with Rockstar. Remember in the closing days of 2023, when Rockstar dropped the first trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Amidst the everything it had going on was a brief shot of a man with extensive facial tattoos, who was quickly called out by people hip to such things as a knockoff of Florida Joker, aka Lawrence Sullivan, a Florida man who went viral for his 2017 mug shot . Sullivan himself called it out in a since-deleted TikTok video, first telling Rockstar " we gotta talk " and then, with no response forthcoming, threatening legal action . Not long after that, though, he put forth a new offer: " Let me voice the character , give me more storyline in the game… Let's make history happen, man." It seems that Sullivan got what he wanted: In a video posted to Instagram, Sullivan said he was given a role in GTA 6 . "I'm an official voice actor on GTA 6, the game." Sullivan says. "For the last three years a lot of people were saying I was not going to be in the game, I was not going to be nothing, they were destroying my mental health. They were saying a lot of fucked shit. But now it's time for me to shit on them and show them what the fuck Florida Joker is about!" "Y'all gonna see. Special voice actor for GTA 6. This ain't no gimmick, this ain't no lie!" I had doubts, but this apparently really ain't no gimmick or lie. Rockstar has posted the full GTA 6 credits and sure enough, Lawrence Sullivan is in there. Now, it could be a different Lawrence Sullivan, sure, but under the circumstances I don't think that's very likely. Sullivan's role doesn't appear to be a particularly prominent one: He's credited, along with a great many other people, as one of "The Local Population." But at the end of the day, he made it: Florida Joker really is in GTA 6, and he seems pretty chuffed about it. I'd call that a happy ending. sources.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
sources.text: "We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us." What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated. Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military. Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today. Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo." And there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out." As each new Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke. "This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years." Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent. It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that. As big as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high." "I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game launched, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam. It's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. " GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

sources.title: Expedition 33 lead writer says Grand Theft Auto 6 layoff concerns show that 'people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value'
sources.text: "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing". Grand Theft Auto 6 is already enormously successful, having enjoyed "the biggest entertainment launch in history" . But the current games industry is such that some Rockstar developers are still concerned about being laid off in the wake of its release. Writing for the Guardian prior to GTA 6 's launch, Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte explained that although there is "no indication that layoffs are coming" it nonetheless "says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off." It might sound odd for the developers of such a hugely successful game to be worried about losing their jobs, but layoffs don't just occur when games or companies struggle commercially. A common cause of layoffs in the games industry is companies trying to reduce overheads after a game has launched, as the studio switches from full production to post-release support for their current game and planning for the next one. It's partly why the industry seems to be in a constant, rolling state of layoffs, even when games appear to sell well. This issue was recently addressed by Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, the lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . Svedberg-Yen, who left Sandfall Interactive in July , claimed that the problem is exacerbated by an imbalance in who benefits financially when a game like Grand Theft Auto 6 launches. "99 Metacritic score. Multiple award nominations before it even released. Massive sales and player engagement. Incredible amounts of tangible and intangible value creation. Yet the team is worried about layoffs," Svedberg-Yen wrote in an Instagram post. "So, who receives the lion's share of the profits from their labor? Not the vast majority of the creative team." Svedberg-Yen pointed out that this is "one of the issues that happens when the people creating the value do not receive a proportionate amount of that value," adding that "In finance, we call that value extraction." Svedberg-Yen also commented on the Rockstar team's ongoing efforts to unionise, with the team in the process of voting on whether or not it wants a union. If successful, the Rockstar Game Workers Union would become the biggest in the UK's gaming sector. "I sincerely hope the Rockstar team is successful in unionizing," Svedberg-Yen wrote. "Layoffs during lulls in development cycles would work a lot better if teams were properly paid for the value they create, not just one-time, but throughout the life of the thing they created." After years of trailers, delays, rumours, and more leaks than Rockstar Games would probably care to count , we can finally get our hands on one of the most anticipated games of all time. GTA 6 is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S , having officially launched on November 19, 2026. And while plenty of players will already have their consoles hooked up and ready to go, there are still some pretty important questions worth asking: which console actually offers the best way to play GTA 6? Is it worth upgrading to a PS5 Pro? And should you even buy a console for it, or simply wait for the inevitable PC release instead ? Look, there's no doubt that the vast majority of players will end up playing GTA 6 on PS5 . Sony's console has a sizeable lead over Xbox Series X|S, with around 95 million PS5 consoles sold , compared with an estimated 35 million Xbox Series X|S consoles . But it's not quite as simple as saying, "play it on PS5, like everyone else." For starters, plenty of people still haven't made the jump to the current generation. If you're still playing on PS4 or Xbox One, GTA 6 could well be the game that finally convinces you to upgrade. Unfortunately, you couldn't have picked a much more expensive time to do it, with console prices, games, storage, and just about everything else seemingly getting pricier by the minute. It's a sign of the times, I'm afraid. Then there's the question of performance. Rockstar's latest open-world adventure is an enormously ambitious game, and the standard PS5 and Xbox Series X|S have their work cut out for them. The PS5 Pro, meanwhile, has considerably more horsepower than the standard PS5, along with PSSR upscaling, making it an interesting option for anyone looking to get the best possible experience. The PS5 Pro is certainly the console I'd be looking at if money were no object. It has a more powerful GPU than the standard PS5, improved ray tracing capabilities, and Sony's PSSR upscaling technology, all of which should help it get more out of demanding games. That doesn't automatically make it a worthwhile upgrade, though. I'd be wary of spending hundreds of dollars extra on a PS5 Pro purely for the promise of better performance in GTA 6 . There's a difference between getting a sharper image or more consistent performance and suddenly unlocking a completely different experience. Whether those improvements justify the considerable price premium is another matter entirely. That being said, if you forced me to give an answer, the PS5 Pro is still probably the best option for getting the most out of GTA 6 on console. If only it wasn't so horrendously expensive, and so difficult to find at a reasonable price right now. If you don't already own a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S , GTA 6 presents a slightly awkward conundrum. On the one hand, this is arguably the biggest game release of the generation ( and probably of all time, quite honestly ), and you're probably going to want to play it ASAP. On the other, buying an entire console for one game is an increasingly expensive proposition in 2026. Sony's current US prices put the PS5 Digital Edition at $599.99 , the standard PS5 with a disc drive at $649.99 , and the PS5 Pro at a frankly eye-watering $899.99 . Microsoft isn't doing much better, with the Xbox Series S now costing $499.99 and the Xbox Series X reaching $749.99 for the digital model or $799.99 with a disc drive. Yikes. Yet, somehow, despite these bonkers prices, there's somehow also an argument for buying sooner rather than later. Console prices have been consistently heading in the wrong direction, and the broader component shortage isn't exactly helping. Major retailers have already warned that console stock could struggle to keep up with demand over the holiday period, with one senior games buyer claiming retailers have been told they won't receive the number of consoles they want ahead of GTA 6's launch. That's not exactly a guarantee that you'll be fighting scalpers for a PS5 come November, though. Sony insists it has secured enough memory to hit its PS5 sales target for the financial year, despite the ongoing component difficulties. Yet, with GTA 6 expected to drive a huge upgrade cycle, I'd rather have my console sorted well before November 19 than find myself scrambling for one at the last minute. Still, if you can, I would still avoid rushing out and paying full price for a console simply because GTA 6 is coming. If you're starting from scratch, keep an eye out for bundles, retailer promotions, trade-in offers, and, particularly as we get closer to November, any GTA 6-specific console deals that might appear. Honestly, refurbished is where I'd be looking right now if you're trying to keep the cost of getting GTA 6-ready as low as possible. You're not going to get much of a discount on brand-new PS5 hardware at the moment, so a reputable refurbished model can make considerably more sense. That's why the next deal I'd consider is a certified refurbished PS5 directly from PlayStation through the PS Direct store . A refurbished PS5 is currently $549, while the refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is $499. If you're happy with digital games, the $499 refurbished PS5 Digital Edition is arguably the most compelling option of the lot, particularly if GTA 6 is the main reason you're buying a console in the first place . That doesn't mean your existing discs suddenly become useless, or that physical games are disappearing overnight, but it does make the $50 saving on a Digital Edition a little more tempting if you're starting from scratch and don't have an existing physical library. sources.text: Choosing whether to sell to Donnie or Brian isn't just about who pays more After the Clean Up After Donnie GTA 6 mission , Donnie becomes a fence you can sell narcotics, marked notes, and jewelry to, all you have to do is drop them in the deposit box at his trailer in Key Lento. But with Brian also a fence, you may be wondering whether it's more beneficial to sell your goods to Donnie or Brian. While one may offer more lucrative rewards, all that glitters isn't necessarily gold in GTA 6 . If you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map , you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry. In GTA 6 Chapter 1 , Donnie (Donnie's Trailer) pays low for narcotics, and very low for jewelry and marked bills. Brian (Brian's Lockup), on the other hand, pays very low for all three types of illicit products. As such, Donnie pays more than Brian for narcotics. For example, if you collect all the cocaine drops Cal tells you about after the Clean Up After Donnie mission and fence them, Donnie offers you $3,400, while Brian offers just $2,720. sources.text: Coffee Break is a relatively straightforward mission, with just a handful of objectives to complete. Coffee Break is the thirty-first mission in GTA 6. GTA 6’s Coffee Break mission sees Jason and Lucia take a moment to plan their next move after their robbery spree in Port Gellhorn. The pair need to earn (or steal) some money before they head back to Vice City. Coffee Break will unlock multiple main and side missions in order to pull this off. For everything you need to know about GTA 6, bookmark our GTA 6 Guide Hub for walkthroughs, top tips and more. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Coffee Break is a very straightforward mission, with just a few things to do.Â From where you start the mission outside the Motel, walk with Lucia towards the motel kitchen, which is located in the southern corner of the property at the mission marker. As you walk to the kitchen, you’ll speak to Wyman, who mentions the Mud Club and its off-road dirt races. This introduces one of the activities you’ll be able to explore later, and point you in the direction of a significant side mission thread. Once you’re inside the kitchen, Lucia will sit down at a table. Head over to the coffee machine and purchase a coffee for Lucia.Â This starts a cutscene in which Jason and Lucia discuss their plans to leave Port Gellhorn and move back to the big smoke, Vice City, to do this, they’re going to need some serious cash. Here you’ll introduced to several potential jobs that can help the pair raise enough money for the move. Don’t worry about which one you select, as all four opportunities will be marked on your map and can be completed in any order. You can also earn cash via the methods you’ve already been using, like shopping shops, and selling cars. Completing Coffee Break unlocks free character switching between Jason and Lucia, allowing you to play as either protagonist outside of specific mission restrictions. This also means that you can free roam as a pair. Alexa, play Hot Together. It also opens four follow-up missions that you can tackle in any order: Thrillbillies, Hit Avery Pawn, Hit Kingpin Bowling and Impounded Vehicle. sources.text: GTA 6 may not have launched with the option to play it entirely in first-person, but where there’s a will, there’s a way. Players have already worked out how to switch from the default third-person perspective, and it requires quite a few fiddly button presses. While you can’t play through the whole of GTA 6 from behind Jason and Lucia’s eyes, there are certain moments where that is a valid option. These include clicking in the right analog stick while holding the left trigger with a weapon unequipped to enter “inspect mode,” which lets you get a closer look at things when standing still. Another instance is when pulling up your phone while driving, which puts you behind the wheel, making steering a bit harder while checking your texts. But now the GTA 6 community has unlocked a way to switch into genuine first-person, allowing you to roam Leonida, fire your guns, and rob stores from much closer to the action. Here’s how to do it, although we can’t guarantee how long this method will last before Rockstar issues a patch fixing it. Note: this appears to currently be working on both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It might take a few tries, but once done, you’ll now be locked into first-person for the rest of your session. Dying won’t reset it, but reloading your save or quitting the game will. Just like the method, the results are by no means perfect, though. It’s a little buggy, with some jank to be found with aiming a weapon, or certain animations not quite agreeing with this glitched version of first-person. It does, however, give us a glimpse of what the future may look like for GTA 6. After all, GTA 5 didn’t receive an official first-person perspective option until it was released on PS4 and Xbox One in 2014, a year after its first launch. And, of course players are already using this forced first-person perspective to try to see Jason and Lucia naked in the shower . Under normal circumstances, can Jason and Lucia get naked in GTA 6? We've got the answer . So, will you be putting this first-person bug to the test? And when do you think Rockstar will include it in an official patch? Let us know in the comments. sources.text: Glitch Grand Theft Auto 6 Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 Outside of aiming with certain weapons, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a strictly third-person game, at least for now. But one player has already found a way to turn on an unofficial first-person mode using a glitch. It’s fairly simple, and players are already using it to creep on Lucia. The trick was shared on YouTube yesterday by glitch hunters oneboyler and OrangeGuy and it’s straightforward enough that anyone should be able to do it. It revolves around spamming a button press while Jason is looking at his phone in his car. The first thing players need to do is go to the controller settings menu and change the touchpad button on the PlayStation 5 DualSense from bringing up the map to controlling the camera. The second thing they need to do his get into a car and pull out Jason’s phone. Here comes the glitch part. You press up on the D-pad to put away your phone and spam the touchpad button while doing so. Try it a couple of times and if you’ve nailed the timing at least once, you’ll be locked in a first-person view once you get out of the car again. The game should stay this way until the next time you shut it off. First Person Lucia in Shower by u/knowledgable_ in GTA I’ve mentioned Jason doing this, but obviously the trick is the same if you’re controlling Lucia. sources.title: Can You Fast Travel in GTA 6?
sources.text: GTA 6 features a massive map that can take some time to traverse if you’re navigating it normally. Of course, plenty of modern open-world video games offer a fast travel system to ease your time on the road, but does GTA 6 follow suit? As it stands, there’s not an extremely viable fast travel option in the game, at least not for free. If you’re wondering how to get across the map more efficiently, here are your travel options in GTA 6. You can purchase Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you still need a copy yourself. It’s a bit of a cop out, but swapping who you’re controlling between Jason and Lucia can technically get you across the map immediately. Once you reach the point in GTA 6 where Jason and Lucia are both playable, you’re able to switch between which of the two you’re controlling. That means that when you swap to the opposite character, you’ll also take control of them wherever they currently are on the map. Oftentimes, the other character will be hanging out around the house, so it can be a quick way to get back home. Or maybe you just want to go mini-golfing, and Lucia is closer to the location than Jason. Swap to her, and hit the (mini) links. While there’s no guarantee that saving, quitting, and reentering the game lands you exactly where you want it to, you can be sure you’ll at least end up somewhere else. Say you’re on a mission that goes south in one way or another, and you end up diving into the ocean and swimming miles away from civilization. Instead of spending the time getting all the way back to shore, just drop a save file and close the game. Upon re-launching, you’ll either be back home, close to a road, or with your vehicle, depending on where the game decides to drop you. It’s not an exact science, but it can get you out of a jam and back to civilization. The most efficient way to travel quickly in GTA 6 is by calling a ride from either Paradise Taxi or RydeMe. Once unlocked, both of these options will be on your smartphone. RydeMe is a dedicated app on your home screen that you’ll open, while Paradise Taxi is accessed via your phone’s contacts list. The benefit of RydeMe is that you can immediately see the cost of your requested ride, while Paradise Taxi doesn’t disclose your fee until the driver shows up at your location. Whichever service you use, you’ll confirm your destination and price once you get in the vehicle. While in motion, you can tell the driver to speed up twice, at the cost of $5 additional dollars each time. For $100, however, you can choose to pay for GTA 6’s actual only means of immediate fast travel once you’re in your ride. If you fork over the money, the game will instantly cut to your driver dropping you off at your chosen destination. It’s not cheap, but it’s your only real option if you can spare the money. Buses and trains also have the ability to pay for immediate fast travel, but by the time you get on either of them, you’ve likely already wasted a lot of time, rendering your “fast traveling” a farce. You can find a bus stop on the map, navigate all the way to it, check the sign for the next bus arrival, wait, board, and then pay the extra fee to fast travel. It’s also a severely limited option in terms of where you can go, as you’ll only be able to be dropped off somewhere on the bus route. Trains work just about the same, only they are even more limited in route options than buses. The train primarily runs in Vice City itself. While it is fairly convenient if you’re in the area and offers immediate fast travel for a fee, it’s also only a viable choice if you have business along the train route itself. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you." After quickly emerging as the highest-rated video game of all time , breaking records across streaming sites , and causing wild spikes in internet traffic , we all kind of knew this was coming. After 13 years, Rockstar has pulled off the greatest score anyone has ever seen. Even in this new update, Take-Two said it was "proud" to help GTA 6 adopt its new crown. It's still got a ways to go before claiming any titles like 'best all-time sales,' but it's a start better than anyone has ever seen in the history of gaming. Just yesterday, it was reported that GTA 6 had managed to sell more than 20 million pre-order copies . Courtesy of Take-Two today, we now know that, somehow, these already staggering numbers actually significantly undershot the reality. The company has now confirmed that it actually moved 32.5 million pre-sale units alone. That's more copies than the vast majority of games have ever sold. sources.text: Preorders of GTA 6 totalled approximately 32.5 million copies. sources.text: "We are incredibly humbled by the response." sources.title: GTA 6 is Getting Review Bombed
sources.text: The critical consensus after GTA 6 ‘s review embargo expired was that Rockstar’s latest entry into the legendary franchise was arguably the new best video game of all time . Still sitting at an insane 99 out of 100 score after 152 official reviews on MetaCritic, it seems GTA 6 is solidified at the top of the pile. But now, a day after the game’s official release date, how are the players actually finding the experience? According to the first batch of user scores coming in on aggregate sites, GTA 6 is either not resonating well with many, or is perhaps the latest victim of review bombing. You can purchase Grand Theft Auto 6 here if you want to judge the game for yourself. Currently on MetaCritic , over 10,000 user scores have poured in for GTA 6 since its launch on November 19, 2026. As it stands, the game has landed at a less-than-impressive 5.1 out of 10 overall score, which certainly isn’t a typical number you’d expect for a game labeled by many critics as the new GOAT. A 5.1 officially labels the game “Mixed” from users on MetaCritic. Out of these 10K+ user scores, nearly 50% are currently “Negative,” however. For a game to be “Negative” on the site, it must be rated below a 50 out of 100. That means that currently, and at least on MetaCritic, about half of GTA 6 users that have logged a score online have rated the game a 49 or below. While opinions are opinions, this also points to the possible reality that GTA 6 is currently being review bombed, with thousands of disgruntled fans/players voicing their thoughts in this manner. Elsewhere, on video game tracking website Backloggd , GTA 6 is faring a little better, though it’s still not exactly rosy. It’s currently sitting at a 3.9 out of 5, which is much better than MetaCritic overall, but still far off from critical acclaim. Out of 492 ratings given by players, 15% of raters have given the game the worst score possible, which is a 0.5 out of 5. So what’s happening with these scores, and what are players upset about? Well, there are many different theories. GTA 6 has had some issues with performance and lost progress , which is sure to be a sore point for some if they’ve had similar issues (though there are also many thousands of players that have had a stable, consistent experience). Delving further into review comments from users, however, is a huge mixed bag that ranges from complaints of too much Red Dead Redemption influence, differing political views, and in some very unfortunate cases, actual racism and sexism. Whatever the reasons may be, there is currently a growing group of GTA 6 players who want their voices heard about their feelings on the game, and they’re taking to the review sites in droves. sources.text: You can fly a GTA 6 jet right at the start of the game by raiding the nearby military base, and here's how to do it Knowing how to get a jet in GTA 6 is essential information if you're planning to cause chaos, as taking control of one of these military aircraft is considered peak criminal behavior. While you'd expect that significant progress in GTA 6 would be required before you even had a chance of swiping such high-end hardware, you can actually go and help yourself to one pretty much as soon as you start the game. To try it yourself, here's how to steal a jet in GTA 6. The location for a number of GTA 6 jets is the Mile Zero Air Station, which is found by heading west along the main road from the starting area, through Abismo Key, then on to Southwind and the military base itself. You can drive there in any vehicle, though I recommend not using your GTA 6 personal vehicle as it will get trashed and left inside the base, so steal a sturdy and reasonably fast vehicle for the job. Purchasing and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation will also improve your odds of surviving the initial stage. Follow the route marked on my map above, which will lead you through some barriers on the road to a set of soldiers who will open fire, then take the first turning right and drive through more soldiers until you see a dirt pile ahead that you can hit to clear the security fences. This is also a Stunt Jump, though you don't need to complete it as long as you clear the perimeter and land on the runway. Once on the runway inside the miliary base, drive straight ahead to where you'll see several GTA 6 jets parked up next to hangars. Pull up alongside one, jump out of your car and hop straight into the cockpit, before firing up the afterburner and turning onto the runway to take off. Once you've taken control of your jet and got airborne, follow the prompt to retract the landing gear and you're away! Be aware that you'll have attracted at least a five-star GTA 6 Wanted Level with this theft, which could go up to six if you start blowing things up, so multiple military jets will be scrambled to shoot you down with homing missiles.
